messages.subject: How to choose normalization?
parts:
Hello MSstats developers,

Firstly, thank you for providing us with Statistical tools and support.

My question regards the best normalization process to choose when dealing with different experiments and datasets. For example, is the experimental design important in the choice of normalization? If I have a basic comparison of two different groups with label free data do I have to apply a different normalization with respect to a time course experiment? Or it depends on the number of proteins involved?

Moreover, I have analyzed a DIA dataset with DIANN, and established a pvalue with a simple T test. Then I ran MSstats on the output of DIANN and the proteins that changed were quite different. Is it possible that this is due to normalization?

Thank you very much again, I wish you a great day,
Giovanni

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: How to choose normalization?
parts:
Hi Giovanni,

Your experimental design/assumptions in your data are very important when choosing the normalization method.

The main question when performing normalization is if you expect the majority of the proteins in your experiment to be changing across conditions or if you expect most to stay the same. If you expect most to stay the same (such as is generally the case in DIA) you are totally fine performing normalization via equalizing the medians (the default option in MSstats). If the experiment is more targeted (SRM/PRM) and you expect to see most of the proteins changing, you will most likely remove true biological variance from your experiment when performing normalization (bad).

The "gold standard" for normalization is to include some spike-in reference standards so that we can normalize to them. This obviously has to be done before you conduct the experiment however.

In terms of your second question, it most definitely has to do with the upstream data processing, not just normalization but how MSstats does missing value imputation, feature selection, and feature summarization. These upstream processing choices have a major impact on your final results.

TLDR; You are probably fine using the default normalization (equalize medians) since your experiment is DIA

Best,
Devon
